definition: ability to stretch and resume shape; adaptability
memoryTip: Like elastic — stretches and snaps back; also flexible response to change.
correctPassage: The market showed surprising elasticity in response to the price change.
wrongPassages: Glass is prized for its elasticity when it shatters at the lightest tap.
The schedule’s elasticity meant every hour was locked and nonnegotiable.
His elasticity of mind rejected every new idea without a second look.

definition: a scarcity or lack of something
memoryTip: Sounds like “death of supply” — a serious lack or shortage.
correctPassage: A dearth of qualified applicants delayed the hire for months.
wrongPassages: A dearth of volunteers filled every shift twice over.
They celebrated the dearth of rain that flooded the valley for days.
The pantry’s dearth of snacks left shelves stacked to the ceiling.

definition: make something seem less important than it is
memoryTip: Play it down — shrink how big or serious something sounds.
correctPassage: Officials tried to downplay the severity of the shortage.
wrongPassages: She downplayed the award by hosting a city-wide parade in her honor.
They downplayed the risk by printing warnings in foot-high red type.
He downplayed the scandal by leaking every detail to the evening news.

definition: surpass; go beyond or move faster than
memoryTip: Strip ahead of the pack — run past and leave others behind.
correctPassage: Demand continues to outstrip the region’s ability to supply housing.
wrongPassages: Sales outstripped the forecast by falling short every single quarter.
Her pace outstripped the field when she finished dead last.
New hires outstripped veterans by needing twice as much coaching.

definition: tendency to stay unchanged; resistance to a change in motion
memoryTip: Newton’s inertia — stays still (or keeps going) until something pushes it.
correctPassage: Institutional inertia made reforming the curriculum slow and difficult.
wrongPassages: The startup’s inertia was famous for reinventing its product every week.
Her inertia showed when she rewrote the plan three times before lunch.
Market inertia meant prices flipped with every rumor by noon.
